title: astra.registry.version/1
description: plugins/<id>/versions/<semver>.json — one release. One file per plugin per version: two authors publishing at the same moment touch two different files, so there is no merge conflict, the review diff is one whole file, and `git log plugins/<id>/` is the audit trail.

published_at.description: The GitHub Release's publication time, UTC, seconds precision. Recorded data, never a clock read at generation time — the index must regenerate byte-identically.

release.description: Where the bytes are served from, and what the artifact URLs are pinned to. `github_release` is what the public catalogue lists: every URL must sit under github.com/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/, so a listing cannot point a plugin's downloads somewhere the named release never was. `direct` exists because a self-hosted or staging catalogue serves its artifacts from its own origin — the daemon was built for exactly that case (Astra `PluginManager::artifact_download_policy` adds the artifact URL's own host to the allow-list) and a schema that could not express it would leave that support unreachable. A `direct` release names a `base_url` and every artifact URL must sit under THAT, so the pinning rule is the same rule with a different anchor; what it does not carry is a named GitHub release, which is why tools/validate.mjs warns and POLICY.md keeps it out of the public catalogue.

base_url.description: kind `direct` only. The https prefix every artifact URL of this release must start with, ending in `/`. https and not http because the daemon's download policy is `https_only()` with no loopback exemption: a plaintext URL would be refused at hop zero on the user's machine, after the listing had already promised it.

protocol.description: Plugin protocol version the bundle speaks (AstraPlugins astra-plugin-sdk/src/protocol.rs PROTOCOL_VERSION).

capabilities.description: The daemon's vocabulary, verbatim (Astra astra-daemon/src/plugins/manifest.rs `Capabilities`). Ten names, no synonyms — `ui_panels` is not one of them.

permissions.description: Phase 4 territory. Present here so the shape is reserved and a listing can carry it before the daemon enforces it; the index copies it through unchanged.

yanked.description: Author withdrew this version. It stays in git and leaves the index. Not a revocation — a revocation is signed, lives in revocations.json, and arrives in Phase 3.

staging.description: Bootstrap only: the release does not exist yet, so there is no digest to pin. tools/validate.mjs REJECTS a staging entry unless --allow-staging is passed. See README.md §The bootstrap entry.

artifacts.description: Platform key -> artifact. The keys are byte-identical to the CLI's --target strings (AstraPlugins astra-plugin-cli, task 2.1) and to the daemon's platform key (Astra registry_client.rs), so nothing has to agree twice. macos-* and *-arm64 are reserved names: Astra ships no daemon for them, so an artifact under those keys would have no host.

artifact.description: sha256 and size are REQUIRED in practice; they are optional here only so a staging entry can be expressed at all. Absent digest means the entry is unverifiable and therefore uninstallable — that rule is enforced in tools/validate.mjs, not in this schema, because the error message matters more than the declaration.

url.description: Any https origin — the release object decides which one. This pattern used to hardcode github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/, which made the GitHub rule unstateable for anything else and so made a self-hosted or staging catalogue inexpressible even though the daemon supports one. The real pinning check outlived the pattern and is stricter than it ever was: tools/validate.mjs requires every URL to start with the prefix its own `release` implies (the release download prefix for github_release, `base_url` for direct) and to end in the declared filename. https, not http: the daemon refuses plaintext before a byte leaves.
